worked_solution:
Newton's second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

The resultant force $F$ acting on $P$ equals the sum of the forces acting on $P.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F & ={F}_{1}+{F}_{2} \\  & =⟨\frac{3t-7}{{t}^{2}-1},\,5t⟩+⟨\frac{7t-3}{{t}^{2}-1},\,5t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{10t-10}{(t+1)(t-1)},\,10t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{10(t-1)}{(t+1)(t-1)},\,10t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{10}{t+1},\,10t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

By Newton's second law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{F}{m} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot ⟨\frac{10}{t+1},\,10t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{t+1},\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the velocity vector $v,$ we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\int a\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{2}{t+1},\,2t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{2}{t+1}\,\text{d}t,\,\int 2t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),\,{t}^{2}⟩+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a (vector) constant of integration. 

We can solve for $C$ by substituting $v=⟨0,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ and $t=0\,\text{s}$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨0,\,-1⟩ & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(0+1),\,{0}^{2}⟩+C \\ ⟨0,\,-1⟩ & =⟨0,\,0⟩+C \\ C & =⟨0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),\,{t}^{2}⟩+⟨0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),\,{t}^{2}-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=1,$ the velocity equals

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+1),\,{1}^{2}-1⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the speed of $P$ when $t=1$ equals the magnitude of $v(1).$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(1)| & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{ln}⁡2)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

The resultant force F acting on P equals the sum of the forces acting on P. Therefore,

F=F1+F2=⟨3t−7t2−1,5t⟩+⟨7t−3t2−1,5t⟩=⟨10t−10(t+1)(t−1),10t⟩=⟨10(t−1)(t+1)(t−1),10t⟩=⟨10t+1,10t⟩.

By Newton's second law, we have

a=Fm=15⋅⟨10t+1,10t⟩=⟨2t+1,2t⟩.

To compute the velocity vector v, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

v=∫adt=∫⟨2t+1,2t⟩dt=⟨∫2t+1dt,∫2tdt⟩=⟨2ln⁡(t+1),t2⟩+C

where C is a (vector) constant of integration.

We can solve for C by substituting v=⟨0,−1⟩m/s and t=0s into the above, as follows:

⟨0,−1⟩=⟨2ln⁡(0+1),02⟩+C⟨0,−1⟩=⟨0,0⟩+CC=⟨0,−1⟩

Therefore, the velocity of P at time t is given by

v=⟨2ln⁡(t+1),t2⟩+⟨0,−1⟩=⟨2ln⁡(t+1),t2−1⟩.

When t=1, the velocity equals

v(1)=⟨2ln⁡(1+1),12−1⟩=⟨2ln⁡2,0⟩.

Finally, the speed of P when t=1 equals the magnitude of v(1). Therefore,

|v(1)|=(2ln⁡2)2+02=2ln⁡2m/s.
